# ISSUE-176 implementation plan

Improve semantic rebase repair by explaining compiler/test locations outside its fixed scope, and allow a maintainer to include those specific safe files for one invocation. This plan changes neither branch targeting nor publication. Implementation must serialize with branch-target work; planning is independent.

## Dimensions

Advisory: medium size, medium uncertainty, high security risk because diagnostic text can influence an edit allowlist. No execution profile is selected. Expected work fits the 16-hour claim budget, including focused security tests and make check.

## What we know

- `internal/pr/rebase_repair.go:151` (`finishResolvedRebase`) obtains trusted configuration at BaseSHA, freezes the PR diff plus conflicted paths in LastRebase.RepairPaths, then validates before each repair. Existing recorded scope wins on retry.
- `internal/pr/rebase_repair.go:23` (`repairAllowed`) checks exact membership and control paths; its protected-path check currently has an AllowHarnessChanges exception. This WorkUnit requires protected paths to remain excluded from repair in every mode.
- `internal/pr/rebase_repair.go:40` (`verifyRepairTree`) checks the entire snapshot; line 64 rejects no-op output. Import is root-bound and rollback-aware; before import the coordinator checks the claim and unchanged clean HEAD.
- `internal/workspace/repair.go:10` computes committed diff paths without rename detection. Preserve this original scope algorithm and the conflicted-path union.
- `internal/validation/check_diagnostics.go:15` bounds displayed diagnostics to 16 KiB/60 lines; capture already attributes plain/JSON test failures. `internal/validation/validator.go:39` exposes check outcomes, including raw untrusted output and infrastructure status. Display text is not authority.
- `internal/lease/rebase.go:18,101,189` stores evidence and applies fenced context updates; fixed RepairPaths cannot be changed after assignment. `internal/fork/coordinator.go:517` accepts contributor rebase-context reports, so rejecting only a CLI flag is insufficient.
- `internal/pr/service.go:820,1019` contains Rebase and trusted resolver construction; `internal/pr/service.go:502` checks approve-task only within the upstream tracker branch; `internal/tracker/local.go:78` separately implements approve-task for OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR. Rebase must explicitly call it on both backends. `internal/cli/pr.go:301` registers resolve flags.
- Existing positive bounded repair and no-publication coverage is `internal/cli/pr_resolve_test.go:394`; scope/no-op rejection is `internal/pr/rebase_repair_test.go:11`.
- Required documentation touchpoints are `docs/developer.md:391-425` and changes/unreleased. No protected configuration changes are authorized.

## What we're assuming

The existing bounded diagnostic capture and repair classification can supply a narrow in-memory location result without changing contributor wire types. Verify through the focused tests below. No stdout text, stored artifact or previous opt-in is authority.

## Open questions

- Git metadata is unavailable (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails); `changes/unreleased/176.md` is absent in this snapshot. Before creating it, inspect the approved base with `git ls-tree`; modify it instead if present there. No other new files are proposed.
- Live GitHub and OCI execution are unavailable here. Fake authorization/CAS and execution-root mapping tests cover the contract without making implementation wait for those environments.

## Design and implementation sequence

1. **Per-run option and authority.** Add proposed boolean `--allow-repair-outside-diff` only to pr rebase, and an Options field. Require --resolve, reject --abort and fork mode before claims, Git mutations, or harness execution. Enforce in Service.Rebase as well as CLI. After pure option validation and fork rejection, always call `s.Tracker.Authorize(ctx, "approve-task")` when the option is set, on BOTH GitHub and local backends, before `openForMutation`, claim acquisition, approval projection, any state mutation, Git operation, or agent work. Fail closed on authorization errors. Do not rely on `remote()` or local operator assumptions. Pass the boolean explicitly into both calls to finishResolvedRebase; never load it from stored evidence, WorkUnit text, instructions, environment, or contributor report.
2. **Bounded capture and compiler authority.** Extend `check_diagnostics.go` and `CheckRunOutcome` with in-memory raw structured locations, separate from escaped display text. Bound storage to 60 entries/16 KiB, paths to 4096 bytes, lines to 8 KiB; mark incomplete/ambiguous results and never accept partial lines. Only failed, completed, non-infrastructure full required checks from the approved-base policy participate. Add an exact command recognizer alongside `parseGoTestAll`: accept only `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` (whitespace tokenization, exactly three tokens); reject flags, wrappers, environment assignments, pipelines, shell operators, substitutions and additional commands. These checks do not execute test bodies. Parse anchored compiler `file:line[:column]:` diagnostics from those outcomes only. Interpret `internal/x/y.go` relative to the check's module-root working directory; root package `./x.go` normalizes to `x.go`. Never prepend a package directory to module-relative compiler paths. Compiler-looking plain go-test output and all test JSON events, including `build-output`, remain display-only for compiler authority. The approved policy already runs build/vet even when another check fails (`validator.go:268-294`); add no compile-only rerun.
3. **Test authority through existing repair diagnosis.** Consume the current coordinator-created `r.Validation.Repair`, bound to the current base/head/check outcomes, generated by `diagnoseRepair`/`classify`/`rerun` (`internal/validation/repair.go:124,186,235`). Require a recognized trusted Go-test command and `TestRegression`: existing targeted candidate rerun selects exactly the attributed package and top-level test, uncached, through the trusted runner; existing base comparison supplies classification. Flaky, pre-existing, unclassified, missing, truncated, unavailable and mismatched summaries grant nothing. Do not rerun classification in PR code. Derive the file from `(package, top-level test)` by AST declaration lookup, NEVER printed `x_test.go:N:` lines or `FAIL` summaries alone. Generalize `candidateDefines`' bounded safe AST reads (`repair.go:278`) to a unique declaration among all tracked `_test.go` files directly in the mapped package directory, reusing `packageDir` (`:307`) and module-boundary checks. Preserve the changed-file-specific use for classification. Add a narrow helper in validation if needed; do not duplicate package/AST logic in PR. Strip subtest suffixes for declaration lookup, reject ambiguous declarations, invalid identifiers and external packages. A P test forging `--- FAIL: TestB` and `FAIL\t<Q>` cannot grant Q's file: targeted Q/TestB passes, hence flaky. Forged file logs within a genuinely failing test can only resolve its own declaration, never the printed file.
4. **Path boundary.** Carry the coordinator-selected execution root with the in-memory check outcome: host/direct or already-isolated runner uses its actual `runner.worktree`; bwrap native and OCI checks use `/workspace` (validator.go:455; sandbox/executor.go:129,142; sandbox/worker.go:266). Map relative compiler paths from that root to host candidate-relative paths. Accept absolute paths only beneath that exact execution root with a component boundary, strip that prefix and resolve against the host worktree; reject host-worktree absolute paths in `/workspace` runs, `/workspace` in host runs, and every other prefix. Never infer roots from output. Canonicalize only well-defined ./ prefixes; reject traversal, drive/UNC/backslash forms, NUL/control characters and escape-bearing paths. Require exact tracked existing .go regular files, reject symlink files and symlink ancestors using root-bound access, and reject paths outside the candidate repository. Apply isControlPath, .git/instruction exclusions, and trusted-base protected patterns unconditionally for repair, even with AllowHarnessChanges. Apply these checks both when building the list and at verification/import; no suffix, directory or alias grants.
5. **Explain before executing.** In finishResolvedRebase after failed-check/infrastructure handling and before the repair-limit check (including limit zero/exhaustion) and before consuming a repair attempt, compare validated locations with the original frozen scope. Without opt-in, any outside location stops repair with a sorted escaped file list, a clear outside-scope reason, last checkpoint and existing fork-aware `swarm pr work <PR>` recovery. Mixed inside/outside failures also stop without opt-in rather than trying inside-only repair; document this recovery-table behavior. With opt-in, blocked/protected locations still stop with manual recovery. Unknown locations never broaden scope. Existing inside-scope failures and no-location failures retain bounded repair and no-op detection.
6. **Ephemeral effective scope and durable evidence.** Keep LastRebase.RepairPaths unchanged. Effective allowlist is original scope plus only corroborated non-protected files named by the current failed validation, under this invocation's opt-in. Recompute after every checkpoint; do not accumulate earlier additions into later attempts or infer them from the now-expanded committed diff. Store bounded sorted additional paths with base/head, attempt/invocation context and explicit opt-in as historical evidence through a dedicated fenced manager method in `internal/lease/rebase.go`. Record before exposing the added scope to the agent. Evidence never authorizes another run. Preserve attempt counters across retries. A later invocation without the flag uses exactly original scope even after an earlier opted-in repair.
7. **Fork boundary and projections.** Keep the maintainer-only evidence method unavailable through the gateway. Reject attempted new opt-in/additional-scope fields in contributor RebaseContext at the coordinator, rather than silently accepting them; do not let old RepairPaths reports replace the original fixed scope. Add no fork operation. Extend RebaseSummary with escaped extra-path evidence; JSON state naturally exposes additive evidence. Never publish during repair or change PR text until explicit submit. Preserve claim fencing, expected head, trusted BaseSHA validation, exact plan gates, snapshot verification and atomic import.
8. **Tests and docs.** Extend files listed below with positive repair, diagnostic-only and adversarial regressions. Update the developer rebasing section/recovery table with the implemented flag and its per-run maintainer behavior, original-scope default, evidence, fork restriction and pr work recovery. Explicitly document in both the changes fragment and rebasing section the deliberate strengthened exclusion: protected/control paths cannot be repaired even for AllowHarnessChanges=true WITHOUT opt-in, as required by this WorkUnit constraint. This narrows that prior exception; AC4 otherwise preserves frozen default scope. Do not change conflict-resolution policy. Add `changes/unreleased/176.md` only after approved-base existence check. Run required checks.

## Exact touchpoints

Modify `internal/cli/pr.go` (rebase flag/validation), `internal/pr/service.go` (Options, Rebase calls/authorization), `internal/pr/rebase_repair.go` (scope/location resolution and repairAllowed), `internal/validation/repair.go` (reuse/generalize packageDir and candidateDefines), `internal/validation/check_diagnostics.go` and `internal/validation/validator.go` (structured capture/outcomes), `internal/lease/rebase.go` (bounded evidence and fenced maintainer-only write), `internal/fork/coordinator.go` (reject contributor widening), `internal/pr/rebase_projection.go` (evidence display), and their existing tests: `internal/cli/pr_resolve_test.go`, `internal/pr/rebase_repair_test.go`, `internal/validation/check_diagnostics_test.go`, `internal/validation/repair_test.go`, `internal/validation/validator_test.go`, `internal/lease/rebase_resolution_test.go`, `internal/fork/fork_test.go`, `internal/pr/rebase_projection_test.go`, `internal/pr/service_test.go`. Reuse existing repair classification without extra compile reruns; keep any small rebase-only helper in these existing files. Modify `docs/developer.md`. Proposed sole new file: `changes/unreleased/176.md` (absent here; approved-base verification outstanding).

## HANDOFF

- Entry points: Options/Rebase `internal/pr/service.go:66,820`; resolver `:1019`; CLI registration `internal/cli/pr.go:301`; finishResolvedRebase/repairAllowed `internal/pr/rebase_repair.go:151,23`; classification/AST/package helpers `internal/validation/repair.go:124,186,235,278,307`; execution root `internal/validation/validator.go:455`; CheckRunOutcome `internal/validation/validator.go:39`; capture `internal/validation/check_diagnostics.go:47,498`; evidence/update `internal/lease/rebase.go:18,189`; fork report admission `internal/fork/coordinator.go:517`; RebaseSummary `internal/pr/rebase_projection.go:17`.
- Extend fixture `TestCLIPRResolvedRebaseBoundedRepairAndNoPublication` and `TestRepairRejectsEntireOutputOutsideFixedScope`, retaining their existing positive and noop cases. Preserve `TestForkContributorResolvesRebaseConflictsAsReports` (`internal/pr/service_test.go:802`) and dropped-path repair coverage (`internal/cli/pr_dropped_paths_test.go:108`).
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/validation -run 'Test.*Diagnostic|Test.*RebaseLocation|Test.*Repair|Test.*CandidateDefines'`; `go test ./internal/pr ./internal/lease ./internal/fork -run 'Test.*Repair|Test.*Rebase|Test.*Fork'`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestCLIPR.*Rebase|TestCLIPRResolvedRebase'`; then `make fmt`, `make check`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`.
- Checked assumptions: source inspection confirmed scope persistence, pre-import claim/head checks, bounded diagnostic capture and fork context transport. Inspection verified LocalTracker approve-task authorization, existing regression reruns/AST mapping, full required-check iteration and /workspace sandbox mapping. Snapshot checks found no fragment 176.md; Git base verification remains outstanding. No tests were run during planning.
- Reopen if package attribution needs broad Go discovery/network execution, recognized build/vet outcomes cannot meet the location boundary, maintainer authority needs a new service, approved-base metadata contradicts file assumptions, or branch-target integration changes the entry points. Reconcile with branch-target work before implementation; do not expand this issue into branch selection or generic diagnosis redesign.
- **What this change breaks:** repository searches found fixed-scope assertions in `internal/pr/rebase_repair_test.go:11` and `internal/cli/pr_resolve_test.go:394`: preserve ordinary default behavior and add opt-in cases plus the deliberate AllowHarnessChanges protected-path exclusion regression. `internal/lease/rebase.go:213` freezes RepairPaths: preserve unchanged, store extensions separately. `internal/fork/testdata/releasedv080/types.go:29` models the released wire format: preserve unchanged; run compatibility tests for additive evidence and unchanged contributor requests. `docs/developer.md:404,423` describes repair scope/recovery: update. `internal/pr/rebase_projection_test.go` checks evidence projection: extend for extra paths without losing human PR text. No instruction templates, protected configuration, fork operation lists, workspace RepairPaths algorithm, or publication call sites need changes.

> Resolve all R1-R4 in REVIEW.md with concrete mechanisms. Always authorize approve-task for opt-in in Service.Rebase on BOTH backends before mutation/claim/Git/agent work; fork widening forbidden. Compiler widening only from recognized exact trusted Go build/vet check, correct execution-root mapping. Test widening only from existing trusted repair classification/rerun plus package/top-level-test AST declaration lookup; forged printed file/FAIL lines never grant authority. Reuse validation repair helpers, avoid extra compile rerun. Explicitly document strengthened protected/control path exclusion even for AllowHarnessChanges without opt-in, as required by constraint; AC4 otherwise preserves scope. Include all reviewer adversarial cases and diagnostics before repair limit. Keep exact outcome scope.

# ISSUE-176 verification plan

Tests must exercise coordinator-created validation outcomes and actual Go output, not only hand-written error strings. Use local and fake GitHub backend fixtures; no live service is required. The following are implementation tests to add or extend, not results already obtained.

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| Compile failure outside repair paths names file and pr work | A tiny Go module where the PR changes a function signature and the rebased target-only caller fails to compile. Run --resolve without opt-in; assert exact nested caller path, outside-scope reason and correct pr work command, no repair agent invocation/attempt consumed, no imported edits or publication. |
| Failing test outside repair paths gets same diagnosis | Target-only nested *_test.go fails after rebase; plain and JSON test attribution feeds existing targeted rerun/classification; only regression-classified tests resolve the unique AST declaration file, never a printed file location. Assert file and recovery command, not repair produced no changes. Include same-basename files in another package and subtests. |
| Maintainer opt-in edits exactly named non-protected files and records them | Repeat compiler/test fixtures with proposed --allow-repair-outside-diff on local and fake GitHub backends. Agent edits original-scope file plus the named caller/test; checks pass and the local checkpoint/evidence contains exact extra paths and source head/base/opt-in. Editing any other file rejects the entire snapshot before import. No remote head or human PR text changes. |
| No opt-in preserves scope | Preserve fixed RepairPaths and existing conflict-path union. Test completed-rebase retry after earlier opted-in checkpoint, scope evidence replay, successive failures naming different files, unchanged attempt budget, and subsequent invocation without flag. Historical extra paths never grant edit permission. Preserve valid original-scope repair and true no-op repair error. |
| make check passes | Run make fmt, make check (vet/staticcheck and race suite), go build ./..., and go test ./... as required by compiled validation policy. Record failures honestly; do not edit trusted policy to bypass checks. |

## Parser and authority regressions

Extend diagnostic capture tests with real plain Go compile output, file:line:column, module-root-relative nested compiler paths and root ./file.go, Go JSON build-output/output/fail events (display-only compiler evidence), bounded very long lines, 60+ locations, huge output, truncation boundaries, malformed JSON, interleaved packages, CRLF, controls/terminal escapes and duplicate locations. Store raw structured paths separately from escaped display text. Successful checks and infrastructure failures never authorize repair.

Exercise tracked regular-file resolution with execution-root-contained absolute paths and ./ prefixes, nested packages, duplicate basenames, missing files, external modules, generated/untracked files, invalid line numbers, traversal, absolute paths outside root, Windows drive/UNC forms, NUL/control/backslash paths, symlink files and symlink ancestor aliases. No ambiguous path, partial token, directory, package name, glob or substring grants files. Protected patterns from the approved base, .git, control paths, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are rejected with and without AllowHarnessChanges and with and without opt-in. Candidate changes to validation policy cannot change the decision.

Adversarial output tests must print forged compiler locations from a test, forged test logs referencing unrelated tracked files in the same and another package, passing-test locations, invented JSON events and log lines that resemble package summaries. Assert they cannot broaden the allowlist solely from their printed strings; exact build/vet recognition plus existing regression rerun and AST declaration lookup must reject them. If attribution is incomplete or bounds are exceeded, verify manual diagnostic recovery and no additions. Do not claim arbitrary stdout is authenticated by regex matching.

## Lifecycle and backend regressions

- CLI and direct service calls reject opt-in without --resolve, with --abort, and in fork mode before agent/Git/state mutations. GitHub non-maintainer authorization fails; local non-maintainer association and GitHub actor without write permission must both fail `approve-task`. Instrument direct Service.Rebase and CLI to assert authorization precedes openForMutation, all Git calls, claims, approval projections, state writes and agent execution. Include successful local OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR and authorized GitHub cases.
- Forge contributor transport requests carrying opt-in/extension fields through invalidate-pr-evidence; the coordinator rejects them. Existing released contributor requests still work. Historical evidence and instructions cannot authorize widening.
- Fenced evidence writes reject stale/expired claims, wrong owner/PR, invalid head/base, excess entries/bytes, invalid paths and mismatched attempt context without partial state changes. Evidence persistence works on local and GitHub CAS stores.
- Change candidate HEAD or dirty state while the agent runs and expire/replace the claim: imports remain rejected with existing detectable claim-fence errors. Preserve import rollback, directory/mode/symlink checks, no partial import after one unauthorized edit, repair limits and explicit submit requirement.
- Keep TestRepairRejectsEntireOutputOutsideFixedScope's noop and valid cases and TestCLIPRResolvedRebaseBoundedRepairAndNoPublication's pass/repair/exhausted/outside/zero/custom cases. Keep fork contributor resolution and dropped-path reporting tests.

## Commands and documentation review

Run focused checks first:

```bash
go test ./internal/validation -run 'Test.*Diagnostic|Test.*RebaseLocation|Test.*Repair|Test.*CandidateDefines'
go test ./internal/pr ./internal/lease ./internal/fork -run 'Test.*Repair|Test.*Rebase|Test.*Fork'
go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestCLIPR.*Rebase|TestCLIPRResolvedRebase'
make fmt
make check
go build ./...
go test ./...
```

Verify the implemented help with `go run ./cmd/swarm pr rebase --help` before documenting the proposed flag. Check developer.md links/anchors and parse edited bash examples with bash -n. Confirm changes/unreleased/176.md is absent at approved base before creating it; otherwise modify the existing fragment. Review the documentation for the per-run maintainer restriction, ordinary unchanged default scope and the deliberate protected/control exclusion even for AllowHarnessChanges=true without opt-in, mixed inside/outside stop behavior, blocked-path recovery and evidence description. No production changes or check execution are part of this planning-only run.

## Required review regressions (R1–R4)

- **Compiler provenance:** Real failed `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` checks authorize only exact canonical files. Passing, infrastructure, fallback/fast-pass, unrecognized/custom checks, `go test`, JSON build-output, wrapper/env/flags/shell compound variants grant no compiler files. Assert no extra compiler rerun occurs. Nested module-root paths must not be doubled with package prefixes.
- **Forged package:** P prints `--- FAIL: TestB` and `FAIL\t<Q>` while Q/TestB is declared outside scope and passes alone. Run real existing targeted rerun, assert flaky classification and no Q widening. Test invented tests, foreign modules and missing attribution similarly.
- **Declaration authority:** A genuine regression logs another tracked test/source filename in its own package and another package; allow only its actual top-level AST declaration. Cover subtests, external-test package declarations, duplicate basenames, duplicate/ambiguous declarations, parse failures, absent declaration, bounded source reads and symlinks. Assert tracked files outside the changed-file list can be located by the generalized helper while candidateDefines classification retains its changed-file semantics.
- **Classification boundary:** Regression after candidate rerun may grant its declaration; flaky, pre-existing, unclassified, rerun timeout/build failure, absent test, exhausted rerun budget, truncated evidence and unavailable/base/head-mismatched summary may not. Consume existing summary; assert no duplicate targeted reruns from PR resolution.
- **Execution root:** Simulate host/direct, already-isolated runner, native bwrap and OCI outcomes. `/workspace/internal/p/x.go` maps correctly only when `/workspace` was selected by the runner. Reject host-prefixed paths for those runs, `/workspace` paths for unrelated host roots, sibling-prefix collisions, traversal after prefix stripping and alternate absolute roots. Relative paths map identically; assert no output-provided root is trusted. Use deterministic runner/argument fixtures; live OCI is not required.
- **Limits and recovery:** Compile/test outside-scope failures name files and the precise fork-aware pr-work command at zero repair limit and after exhaustion, before any agent invocation or attempt increment. Mixed inside/outside failures without opt-in stop entirely. With opt-in but no remaining attempts, print the outside-file diagnosis alongside repair-limit context and grant nothing.
- **Protected exception removal:** Matrix AllowHarnessChanges true/false × opt-in true/false, including protected files already in original RepairPaths. Assert construction and whole-tree verification/import reject protected/control paths in every combination; no partial import. This deliberately strengthens prior default harness-change behavior; all other AC4 original-scope assertions remain.
- **Evidence/wire boundary:** Store new opt-in/extensions in a separate evidence struct and fenced manager method, never fields in RebaseContext; keep releasedv080 types unchanged. Attempt contributor widening through direct service and raw transport, including unexpected opt-in/extension fields; reject before mutation. Do not add a fork operation. Run existing released-wire compatibility tests.
